title: Optimizing the accuracy of cortical volumetric analysis in traumatic brain injury
author: Diamond, Donald, et al.

steps.title: Run FreeSurfer recon-all
steps.instruction: Process the patient's MRI with FreeSurfer's standard recon-all pipeline. Include the -bigventricles option for subjects with enlarged ventricles. If a T2‑weighted image is available, add the -T2pial or -FLAIRpial option. If recon‑all and classic manual edits have already been completed, skip to step 3.

steps.title: Manual edit FreeSurfer outputs
steps.instruction: Spend approximately 30 min reviewing the recon‑all results, edit necessary volumes (e.g., brainmask.mgz, wm.mgz) to correct surface inaccuracies, then re‑run recon‑all to apply the edits. Repeat until surfaces are satisfactory. The addition of a T2‑weighted image may reduce editing time. See the FreeSurfer Guide to Recon Editing for troubleshooting.

steps.title: Launch FreeView with surfaces
steps.instruction:
Open the development version of FreeView and load the subject's T1.mgz together with the left‑hemisphere (lh.pial) and right‑hemisphere (rh.pial) pial surface files. Turn curvature off and hide 3‑D slices. Use the following command (add -layout 4 if desired):
freeview -v $SUBJECTS_DIR/mri/T1.mgz -f $SUBJECTS_DIR/surf/lh.pial:curvature_method=off -f $SUBJECTS_DIR/surf/rh.pial:curvature_method=off -hide-3d-slices

steps.title: Set horizontal layout
steps.instruction: Select the “1 & 3 Horizontal” layout from the view‑panel toolbar (or include -layout 4 in the freeview command).

steps.title: Identify lesion‑crossing surfaces
steps.instruction: Scroll through the loaded T1.mgz (and T2raw.mgz or FLAIRraw.mgz if available) to locate any reconstructed pial surfaces that pass through cortical lesions. Record each lesion for labeling in the next steps.

steps.title: Label lesion on pial surface
steps.instruction: Create, close, fill, and save a lesion label for each identified cortical lesion.

substeps.instruction: Click the “Custom Fill” button, choose “Make Path”, and left‑click along the appropriate hemisphere’s pial surface (lh.pial or rh.pial) to place a continuous chain of points outlining the lesion.
Click the “Make Closed Path” button to close the outline.
Click “Clear Marks", then place a single point inside the closed contour and click “Custom Fill” → “Fill" to generate the lesion label.

In the Label Index, click “Save" and name the file with the hemisphere prefix (lh. or rh.) followed by "lesion‑??.label" where ?? is a zero‑padded integer from 01 to 99 (e.g., lh.lesion-01.label). Repeat for every cortical lesion.

steps.title: Generate corrected statistics
steps.instruction: Run the provided correct_segstats.sh script (available at https://github.com/ComaRecoveryLab/Lesion_Correction). The script merges all lesion‑??.label files per hemisphere into overlay files (??.all-lesions.mgz) using mris_label2annot and mris_annotation2label, applies mris_anatomical_stats to compute cortical volume measurements while ignoring regions within the lesion overlays, and finally creates per‑hemisphere tables with aparcstats2table.
